issues.description: The problem statement specifies calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (explicitly asking for double precision), but the solution implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This mismatch between the specified return type and the provided implementation will confuse students about the expected signature and precision of the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent: either update the problem statement to request an int return type and remove references to double precision, or change the implementation (and template guidance) so calculateTotalPrice returns a double and computes the total using double arithmetic. Ensure the template and solution use the same return type as the specification.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but it also requires the stock attribute to be static (and earlier describes it as final). Initializing a static final stock in an instance constructor is contradictory (a static final field must be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer). This creates an impossible-to-follow instruction about where and how to initialize the static/final stock field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design: either (A) make stock a static (and possibly final) field that students should initialize at declaration or in a static initializer (update the instructions to not require constructor initialization), or (B) make stock an instance final field initialized in the constructor and remove the requirement that it be static. Update the problem statement and template to match the chosen approach so students have a single consistent initialization instruction.
